meta.location: The Nephite cities, the east wilderness, and the land of Morianton

world_behind.title: Moroni does not stop after winning
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has him start the twentieth year by digging heaps of earth around every city. The victory of Alma 49 changes nothing about the programme.

world_behind.title: The works are given in four layers
world_behind.text: Verses 2 through 4 stack ridges of earth, timbers to the height of a man, a frame of pickets, and towers with covered places on top.

world_behind.title: He clears and then settles the east wilderness
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 9 drive the Lamanites out and move Zarahemla's people in. Holding ground means putting inhabitants on it.

world_behind.title: The armies grow because of the works
world_behind.text: Verse 12 says they increased daily because of the assurance of protection the fortifications gave. Building attracts recruits.

world_behind.title: New cities are named after living men
world_behind.text: Verse 13 names a city Moroni; verse 14 names Nephihah; verse 15 names Lehi. The record gives no comment on the practice.

world_behind.title: A land dispute nearly becomes a migration
world_behind.text: Verses 25 through 29 have Morianton's people claim part of Lehi, take up arms, and then plan to flee north when Moroni's army looks likely.

world_behind.title: A beaten servant changes the outcome
world_behind.text: Verses 30 and 31 have Morianton assault a maid servant, who escapes to Moroni and reports the plan. Mormon says the flight would have been lamented.

words.text: Pointed stakes set upright in a defensive frame. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible, both in this chapter. Mormon puts them on top of the timbers and calls them strong and high.

Fortified positions. The word occurs fourteen times in this record and never in the King James Bible, and most of them are in these war chapters. Verse 6 says Moroni made one of every city in all the land.
Mourned aloud. The word occurs once in this record and eleven times in the King James Bible, usually of formal mourning for the dead. Mormon uses it for what a northward migration would have been.
Strong feeling, and here uncontrolled temper. Mormon calls Morianton a man of much passion in the verse that has him beating a servant, and the phrase is his explanation of why the plan failed.

Moral straightness. The record uses the noun twice and the King James Bible nineteen times, mostly in Psalms and Proverbs. Mormon uses it of Nephihah filling the judgment-seat, in the verse recording his death.
A formal rite that binds. Pahoran takes the seat with an oath and a sacred ordinance to judge righteously, keep the peace and freedom, and grant the people their worship.

phrases.term: Works of timbers built up to the height of a man
phrases.text: Mormon gives a measurement rather than an impression. The whole description in verses 2 through 4 is written the way a builder would describe it.

phrases.term: Places of security to be built upon those towers
phrases.text: Covered positions above the pickets, so that stones and arrows could not reach the men throwing them. The design puts the defenders where they can strike and cannot be struck.

phrases.term: Thus Moroni did prepare strongholds against the coming of their enemies, round about every city
phrases.text: The summary of a five-year programme in one line. Alma 49 had shown two cities; this verse extends it to all of them.

phrases.term: He caused that the inhabitants... should go forth into the east wilderness and possess the land
phrases.text: Clearing the ground is half the operation and settling it is the other half. Moroni moves civilians into the emptied wilderness as the way of keeping it.

phrases.term: Which did increase daily because of the assurance of protection which his works did bring forth
phrases.text: Mormon connects the engineering to recruitment. People joined the armies because the fortifications made service look survivable.

phrases.term: They called the name of the city Moroni
phrases.text: A city named for the living commander. Mormon records it without remark, and Alma 51 and 62 both turn on what happens to that city.

phrases.term: They were not in the wrong
phrases.text: Mormon settles the land dispute in five words. The people of Lehi appealed to Moroni, and the record settles the merits before describing the response.

phrases.term: Morianton being a man of much passion, therefore he was angry with one of his maid servants, and he fell upon her
phrases.text: The assault is reported plainly and given a cause. Mormon puts it in the verse that begins with what would have happened otherwise.

phrases.term: She fled, and came over to the camp of Moroni, and told Moroni all things
phrases.text: An unnamed woman carries the intelligence that stops a migration. Her escape is the hinge of the second half of the chapter.

phrases.term: Which consequences would lead to the overthrow of their liberty
phrases.text: Moroni's reasoning for intercepting a group that only wanted to leave. Mormon gives the strategic argument rather than a claim about wrongdoing.

phrases.term: Upon their covenanting to keep the peace they were restored to the land of Morianton
phrases.text: The settlement after the battle. The defeated are given their lands back on a promise, and a union takes place between them and the people of Lehi.

verses.label: v. 1–6
verses.title: The works
verses.text: Moroni keeps preparing. Heaps of earth around every city, timbers to the height of a man on top of the ridges, a frame of pickets on the timbers, towers overlooking the pickets, and covered places on the towers from which stones could be cast. A stronghold at every city in the land.

verses.label: v. 7–12
verses.title: The border
verses.text: He drives the Lamanites out of the east wilderness, settles Zarahemla's people there to the seashore, and places armies on the south with fortifications. He cuts off the Lamanite strongholds east and west and fortifies the whole line, and his armies grow daily because the works make protection look real.

verses.label: v. 13–16
verses.title: New cities
verses.text: They found a city called Moroni by the east sea, a city called Nephihah between Moroni and Aaron, and many in the north, one called Lehi by the seashore. Mormon notes the naming and moves on.

verses.label: v. 17–24
verses.title: Prosperity
verses.text: Mormon breaks off to describe the years of peace: the Nephites prospering exceedingly, the church established, the people blessed according to the promise, and no happier people among all those created by the hand of God.

verses.label: v. 25–29
verses.title: The dispute
verses.text: In the twenty-fourth year, Morianton's people claim part of Lehi and take up arms. Lehi's people flee to Moroni and appeal, and Mormon says they were not in the wrong. Fearing Moroni's army, Morianton plans to take his people north.

verses.label: v. 30–33
verses.title: The servant
verses.text: He beats a maid servant in a temper. She escapes to Moroni's camp and reports everything, including the plan to flee. Moroni fears the northern people would join them and that the consequences would overthrow Nephite liberty, so he sends an army.

verses.label: v. 34–40
verses.title: The interception, and Pahoran
verses.text: Teancum heads them at the narrow pass by the sea, kills Morianton, defeats and takes his army, and brings them back. On covenanting peace they are restored to their lands and united with Lehi. Nephihah dies having judged uprightly, and his son Pahoran takes the seat under oath.

chapter.title: The fortifications are described like a specification
chapter.text: Earth, timbers, pickets, towers, covered positions, in that order with a height given. Mormon writes four verses of construction detail and no rhetoric.

chapter.title: Holding land means living on it
chapter.text: Moroni empties the east wilderness and then moves families into it. The military operation is completed by a settlement programme.

chapter.title: Security recruits
chapter.text: Verse 12 says the armies grew daily because the works assured protection. Building the defenses solved the manpower problem as a side effect.

chapter.title: Five peaceful years get eight verses
chapter.text: Verses 17 through 24 describe prosperity, church growth, and a claim that no people were happier. Mormon gives the good years room before the dispute.

chapter.title: The record decides the land case
chapter.text: Verse 27 says the people of Lehi were not in the wrong. Mormon rarely rules on a dispute and does it here in a subordinate clause.

chapter.title: A servant's escape prevents a national loss
chapter.text: Morianton's temper cost him the plan, and an unnamed woman carried it to Moroni. Mormon marks the migration as something that would have been lamented.

chapter.title: The interception is justified strategically
chapter.text: Moroni's reason is what a northern alliance would do to Nephite liberty. The record gives the argument rather than asserting that leaving was a crime.

chapter.title: The defeated get their land back
chapter.text: Morianton dies and his people covenant peace and are restored. The chapter that begins with walls ends with a union between two contending groups.

applications.title: Keep building after the win
applications.text: Moroni started a new fortification programme the year after a total victory. When something has just gone well, that is the moment to extend the work rather than bank it.

applications.title: Make the protection visible
applications.text: People joined because they could see the walls. When you want others to commit to something risky, show them what has been done to make it survivable.

applications.title: Settle what you have cleared
applications.text: Driving the enemy out was half of it. After you have fixed a problem, put something in the space so it does not simply return.

applications.title: Listen to the person who ran
applications.text: A beaten servant brought the information that changed the outcome. When someone arrives with an account of what is happening, hear them out regardless of their standing.

questions.text: What did I stop maintaining once the pressure came off?
Where am I exposed while trying to help others?
Does what I have built make people more willing to join me?
Whose dispute have I refused to judge because judging is uncomfortable?
What has my temper cost me that I have not counted?
Who has told me something true that I nearly dismissed?
Whom have I restored after they were in the wrong?
